rows.name: MAKELEVEL

cells.Where: `make` (`GNUmakefile`). `bin/ci/test-make-environment-guidance.sh` removes it for `make` commands that it starts.
cells.What Tron does with it: The makefile prints its warning about a run outside the Nix dev shell only when the value is `0`.

evidence: GNUmakefile:1 - the warning block applies only when `IN_NIX_SHELL` and `CI` are both empty
GNUmakefile:2 - `ifeq ($(MAKELEVEL),0)` guards both `$(warning ...)` pairs; this is the only read
GNUmakefile:3-9 - the warning also needs no goal, or a goal other than `deb`, `deb-host`, `gen-deb/%`
bin/ci/test-make-environment-guidance.sh:32-33 - `env ... -u MAKELEVEL -u MFLAGS` on the first `make --question lint` command
bin/ci/test-make-environment-guidance.sh:42 - the same removal on the second command; lines 54-55 and 66-67 on the third and fourth
GNUmakefile:878 - `make test-lint` runs the script, so the script can inherit a `MAKELEVEL` above 0

rows.name: MAKEOVERRIDES

cells.What Tron does with it: GNU Make stores the variable assignments of the `make` command line in it. For a remote build, the makefile adds them to the `make` command on the LSF worker. It leaves out `REMOTE`, `REMOTE_HOST`, `REMOTE_MODEL` and `NPROC_BUILD`.

evidence: GNUmakefile:394-396 - `REMOTE_BUILD_OVERRIDES = $(filter-out REMOTE=% REMOTE_HOST=% REMOTE_MODEL=% NPROC_BUILD=%,$(MAKEOVERRIDES))`, plus `-B` when the caller passed it; this is the only read
GNUmakefile:397-399 - with `REMOTE_ENABLED`, the build goals run `bin/bsub-build make $@ $(REMOTE_BUILD_OVERRIDES)`
bin/bsub-build:53-60 - the payload runs the given command on the worker inside `nix develop`, with `REMOTE=0` and `NPROC_BUILD=<cores>`
bin/bsub-build:74-75 - `bsub -I` submits the payload to LSF

evidence: bin/ci/test-make-environment-guidance.sh:33 - `-u MAKELEVEL -u MFLAGS` on the first `make --question lint` command

rows.name: NIX_BUILD_CORES

problems.statement: Sets the number of parallel jobs in 3 Nix builds
problems.code_says: Each build caps the number at 16 jobs, and uses 1 job when the variable is unset. `tron-cmake-test-build` takes the smaller of the value and `NPROC_BUILD` (16). `nix/model-traces.nix` caps at 16. `generate.py` and `export.py` cap at `MAX_GENERATION_JOBS = 16` and `MAX_EXPORT_JOBS = 16`.

problems.statement: `ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh`, `generate.py`, `export.py` and 3 Nix build files (... and 3 more files)
problems.code_says: The cell counts files. The three Nix files read the variable first. `nix/model-plugins.nix` and `nix/model-traces.nix` always pass `--jobs`, so the read in `generate.py` and `export.py` only gives the default of a run without `--jobs`.

cells.Where: `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix`, `nix/model-plugins.nix`, `nix/model-traces.nix` and other files. `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` also sets it for `bin/ci/ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh`.
cells.What Tron does with it: The value sets the number of parallel jobs in the Nix builds `tron-cmake-test-build` (Ninja jobs), `tron-generated-test-models` (model plugin generation) and `tron-test-model-traces` (model trace export). Each build caps the number at 16 jobs. Unset: 1 job.

evidence: nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix:127-132 - reads `${NIX_BUILD_CORES:-1}`, then sets `NIX_BUILD_CORES` and `NPROC_BUILD` for `bin/ci/ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh`
nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix:37 - `NPROC_BUILD = 16`; line 136 passes the selected number to `cmake --build -j`
bin/ci/ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh:4 - `nix_build_cores=${NIX_BUILD_CORES:-1}`; lines 7-11 reject non-digits with exit status 2; lines 17-22 raise 0 to 1 and cap at `NPROC_BUILD`
nix/model-plugins.nix:22-25 - `jobs="${NIX_BUILD_CORES:-1}"`, a value of 0 or less becomes 1; line 31 passes `--jobs "$jobs"`; line 9 is the pname `tron-generated-test-models`
nix/model-traces.nix:27-32 - the same read, 0 or less becomes 1, above 16 becomes 16; line 40 passes `--jobs "$jobs"`; line 9 is the pname `tron-test-model-traces`
bin/ci/model-plugins/generate.py:234 - `--jobs` default is `os.environ.get("NIX_BUILD_CORES", "1")`; lines 218-225 cap at `MAX_GENERATION_JOBS`, which line 30 sets to 16

bin/ci/model-traces/export.py:327-328 - `_default_jobs()` reads `NIX_BUILD_CORES` with default `1`; line 336 calls it when the parser is built; lines 317-324 cap at `MAX_EXPORT_JOBS`, which line 23 sets to 16

rows.name: NIX_NO_SELF_RPATH

cells.Where: No reader in Tron. `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` sets it for `stdenv` (the standard build environment of Nix packages).

rows.name: OMP_NUM_THREADS

problems.code_says: The cell does not say in which way. The makefile runs `nproc`. With `OMP_NUM_THREADS=N`, `nproc` prints N and not the number of available CPUs, also when N is higher. Measured with GNU coreutils 8.32 on a host with 6 available CPUs: `OMP_NUM_THREADS=3 nproc` prints 3, `OMP_NUM_THREADS=64 nproc` prints 64, and the values `0`, `abc` and empty print 6.

cells.What Tron does with it: With a positive value, `nproc` prints that value and not the number of available CPUs. The makefile takes the default of `NPROC_BUILD` (the number of parallel build jobs) from the `nproc` output and caps it at 16 jobs.

evidence: GNUmakefile:95-97 - `ifndef NPROC_BUILD` then `NPROC_BUILD := $(shell n=$$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 16); echo $$(( n < 16 ? n : 16 )))`
git grep -n OMP_NUM_THREADS (commit 7eddde7895) - no file except README.env-vars.md holds the name; the read happens inside `nproc`

measurement on the agent host, `nproc` of GNU coreutils 8.32, 6 available CPUs - `OMP_NUM_THREADS=3` prints 3, `=64` prints 64, `=0`, `=abc` and empty print 6, `OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=2` prints 2

rows.name: OMP_THREAD_LIMIT

problems.code_says: The value is an upper limit of the `nproc` output. It lowers the default only when it is below the number of available CPUs and below 16. Measured with GNU coreutils 8.32 on a host with 6 available CPUs: `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=2 nproc` prints 2 and `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=64 nproc` prints 6.

cells.What Tron does with it: With a positive value, `nproc` prints at most that value. The makefile takes the default of `NPROC_BUILD` (the number of parallel build jobs) from the `nproc` output and caps it at 16 jobs.

evidence: GNUmakefile:95-97 - `ifndef NPROC_BUILD` then `NPROC_BUILD := $(shell n=$$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 16); echo $$(( n < 16 ? n : 16 )))`
GNUmakefile:93-94 - the only match of the name in code is a comment; the read happens inside `nproc`
measurement on the agent host, `nproc` of GNU coreutils 8.32, 6 available CPUs - `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=2` prints 2, `=64` prints 6, `=0` prints 6

rows.name: RHOST

cells.What Tron does with it: The target `rinstall` copies the `iotools` binary (a third-party tool that reads and writes hardware registers) to `<RUSER>@<RHOST>:<SBINDIR>` with `scp`. It then runs `<SBINDIR>/iotools --make-links` on that host with `ssh`. Unset or empty: the target copies nothing.

evidence: bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile:55 - `RHOST ?=` keeps a value from the environment or the command line
bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile:56-62 - with a non-empty `RHOST`, `scp $^ $(RUSER)@$(RHOST):$(SBINDIR)` then `ssh $(RUSER)@$(RHOST) $(SBINDIR)/$(BINARY) --make-links`; otherwise only an `echo`
bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile:41 - `BINARY=iotools`; line 39 `SBINDIR ?= /usr/local/sbin`; line 54 `RUSER ?= root`
bin/iotools-1.5/README:20-22 - the iotools README describes `rinstall`, `RHOST` and `RUSER`
bin/iotools-1.5 - the sources `mmio_rw.c`, `msr.c`, `pci_rw.c`, `io_rw.c`, `cmos_rw.c`, `smbus_rw.c` show the register commands of the tool

unresolved: NIX_NO_SELF_RPATH - the checkout holds no reader, so the sentence about the run path rests on nixpkgs behavior that was not read here. Source that settles it: `pkgs/stdenv/generic/setup.sh` (function `_addRpathPrefix`) and `pkgs/build-support/setup-hooks/multiple-outputs.sh` at the nixpkgs revision that `flake.lock` pins. If that source differs, cut the second sentence of the last cell.

OMP_NUM_THREADS, OMP_THREAD_LIMIT - the rows describe `nproc`, not Tron code. The behavior was measured with GNU coreutils 8.32 on the agent host only. Measurement that settles it for the build hosts and the Nix dev shell: `nproc --version` and `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=2 nproc` there.

OMP_THREAD_LIMIT - who sets it. Only a makefile comment (GNUmakefile:93-94) says that LSF sets it to the reserved cores. No code in the checkout sets it, so the row does not say it. Measurement that settles it: `env` inside an LSF job on the lab installation.

(2) Counts removed: MFLAGS ('4 `make` commands') and NIX_BUILD_CORES ('3 Nix build files', 'and 3 more files', '3 Nix builds'). (3) Source comment removed: NIX_NO_SELF_RPATH. The new text states what the value does and the `disallowedReferences` attribute of the same build. (4) Glossary: MAKEOVERRIDES no longer defines 'remote build'. RHOST now defines iotools. (5) Content: NIX_BUILD_CORES gains the 16-job cap and the unset case, and its Where cell now names the three Nix files that read the variable first. OMP_NUM_THREADS and OMP_THREAD_LIMIT now say what `nproc` does with the value. RHOST gains the unset case. MAKELEVEL is graded correct, and its Where cell gains the test script that removes the variable, as the MAKEFLAGS and MAKECMDGOALS rows already list that script. The MFLAGS row no longer carries that fact. NIX_BUILD_CORES: the row says 'Unset: 1 job' and does not cover `0` or an empty value. The two Nix files turn those into 1 job, but `bin/ci/model-traces/export.py` evaluates `_default_jobs()` when it builds its parser (line 336), also when `--jobs` is given. Read from the code, not run: with `NIX_BUILD_CORES=0` or an empty value in the environment that call raises `argparse.ArgumentTypeError` outside the argparse type handling. The developer-reader hint on the two OMP rows asks for a move to table 7.3. The input already places both rows in 7.3, so no cell changed for it. Not changed, for the author to decide: (a) NIX_CFLAGS_COMPILE and NIX_NO_SELF_RPATH are names of nixpkgs (the Nix package collection: its compiler wrapper and its `stdenv`), not of the `nix` program. 'Defined by' keeps 'Nix' as the document uses that word for the whole tool set. (b) 'One test' stays in the NIX_CONFIG and NIX_REMOTE rows. It names a single test and is not a number that the validator rejects. (c) OMP_NUM_THREADS appears nowhere in Tron code, and OMP_THREAD_LIMIT only in a makefile comment.
